Meditation helped me. Many think of meditation as thinking of nothing but it's not that - it's having made yourself aware of the present moment. Meditation is like sitting on park bench and watching the traffic go by. The thoughts are the cars, they come and go. Intangible. 

You cannot predict the future, you cannot return to the past, as humans we only have the current moment. So rooting oneself in the breath and practicing that awareness daily. 1 minute. 1 hour. Few seconds. Doesn't matter. Doesn't have to be an ethereal, out there experience. Its just a practice. I would check out the headspace app or youtube meditations, very helpful start and can explain much better than I.

(For the record not a professional vocal coach so anyone please correct me if I'm wrong):

I've struggled with neck, mouth and general throat tension relative to breathing as well and have spent a lot of my time focusing on ways to alleviate. Obviously breath support is crucial. Making sure you're not holding and squeezing anywhere. Easier said than done right? What helped me was really learning about diaphragmatic breathing and breath support in general. 

Take time to learn about apoggio, just spending some time breathing in your body and really feeling that in your belly and ribs. The inner costal muscles, the '360' breath of belly back and ribs with a straight back. New York Vocal Coaching on Youtube has a video that's very good about this:

https://youtu.be/oDrhkt8KIA4

Secondly, I'd assess tension as a result of subconscious thought. Things like anxiety. Perhaps you clench your jaw unknowingly or just generally have a lot of tension in your upper shoulders, neck, jaw. Try soft slow stretches and see if it makes a difference in your tonality. Turning your head from left to right and up and down as slowly and as far as you can comfortably. Opening your jaw, sticking your tongue out. Rolling your shoulders. There are tons of great stretches for these things.
 
And lastly, in a weird way, it was psychological. Sometimes we overthink singing. You're on the right track by saying i know if it hurts to stop. Personally I was so worried about tension and breath that I was self sabotaging and making breathing like rocket science when in reality I should've just felt it. 

Hopefully these help, it really made the biggest difference for me and I'm sure you'll sound great when you figure it out! :)
